svg.title: Taurine and aging: what has actually been tested
svg.desc: Taurine and aging: what has actually been tested. Approved uses: Prescription drug in Japan for heart failure, a liver indication and MELAS (2019); a supplement in the US. Verdict: Drug in Japan only. Lifespan in animals: 10-12% longer average life in one 2023 mouse study; healthier mice in 2023 and 2026 studies. Verdict: Animal signals. Does blood taurine fall with age?: Yes (Science 2023); rises or flat in people (NIA-led 2025, Yale-led Cell 2026). Verdict: Disputed. Lifespan or aging in people: No lifespan trial; one 6-month biological-age trial finished, no results posted. Verdict: Not tested. Blood pressure, sugar, lipids: Meta-analyses of small RCTs: modest drops in blood pressure, glucose and lipids. Verdict: Modest signals. Older or sick patients: Hip fracture (2015) and cirrhosis fatigue (2026) trials missed their main goals. Verdict: Mostly negative. Thinking and memory: 2025 and 2026 reviews: no clear cognitive benefit from taurine alone. Verdict: No clear effect. Safety: Short trials report few side effects; a 2025 mouse study tied taurine to leukemia growth. Verdict: Open questions.
